description.fun: Corsola's coral branches glitter in seven colours in the sunlight and grow back overnight if one snaps off, which helps, since people keep them as charms for safe childbirth and prize its horn for jewellery. It needs clean water, and its colonies can grow so big that Pacifidlog Town is built on top of them. In Alola it snaps off branches to distract hungry Mareanie.
description.guide: A Water- and Rock-type coral Pokémon that lives in warm, clean seas and regrows lost branches overnight. It does not evolve, but its Ghost-type Galarian form, a bleached coral spirit, evolves into Cursola.
description.tagline: Living coral that regrows overnight and holds up a whole town

description.fun: Galar's Corsola were wiped out by sudden changes in climate and ocean temperature and came back as ghosts: bleached white, frowning, with see-through branches that drain the life force of anyone they take root in. It's easily mistaken for a rock, but it curses anyone who kicks it by accident.

Cursola is what a Galarian Corsola becomes after soaking up so much spirit energy that its shell breaks open and ghostly ectoplasm pours out. Touch that ectoplasm and you turn stiff as stone, a power that may nod to the Gorgons of Greek myth. Under a full moon, Cursola gather and send their branches into the sky, and nobody yet knows why.
description.guide: A Ghost-type Pokémon introduced in Generation 8, the evolution of Galarian Corsola, made of ectoplasm bursting from a broken coral shell. Touching its ectoplasm leaves people stiff as stone. It is based on bleached coral, and its name combines 'curse' and 'Corsola'.
description.tagline: A bleached coral ghost whose touch turns you to stone

note.text: Only Galarian Corsola evolves into Cursola, at level 38; Corsola from anywhere else doesn't evolve.
